target.title: fix(agents): web_fetch leaves body open after provider fallback
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where `web_fetch` could leave an upstream response body open when a non-OK (or extraction-failed) response was abandoned after a successful provider fallback return. `finally` only called `release()`; the unread (or abandoned) body was never cancelled.

## Why This Change Was Made

Before returning a provider-fallback payload that abandons the direct fetch response, cancel the response body best-effort (`body?.cancel().catch(...)`), matching the cancel-before-release campaign used elsewhere in core. Covers both the non-OK early-return path and the readability-disabled HTML fallback return path.

## User Impact

**Before:** Successful provider fallback after a non-OK upstream (or after skipping local HTML extraction) could retain an abandoned response stream until GC.

**After:** The abandoned upstream body is cancelled before returning the fallback payload; dispatcher release still runs in `finally`.

## Evidence

### Proof (exit 0)

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/tools/web-fetch.provider-fallback.test.ts -t "cancels an unread non-OK|cancels the response body when readability" --reporter=verbose
```

```text
stdout | ... > cancels an unread non-OK response body when provider fallback succeeds
[web-fetch non-ok fallback cancel proof] cancelled=true extractor=custom-provider

stdout | ... > cancels the response body when readability-disabled fallback succeeds
[web-fetch readability-off fallback cancel proof] cancel_invoked=true extractor=custom-provider

 ✓ |agents-core| ... > cancels an unread non-OK response body when provider fallback succeeds 232ms
 ✓ |agents-core| ... > cancels the response body when readability-disabled fallback succeeds 11ms
 ✓ |agents-tools| ... > cancels an unread non-OK response body when provider fallback succeeds 375ms
 ✓ |agents-tools| ... > cancels the response body when readability-disabled fallback succeeds 18ms

 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  4 passed | 10 skipped (14)
```

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Non-OK and readability-disabled HTML upstream bodies are cancelled when provider fallback succeeds and returns early.
- **Canonical reachability path:** `createWebFetchTool` → fetch → `maybeFetchProviderWebFetchPayload` success → `cancelUnreadWebFetchBody(res)` → return payload → `release()`.
- **Boundary crossed:** Abandoned upstream HTTP body stream → `body.cancel()` before fallback return (non-OK unread path + readability-off path).
- **Shared helper / provider constraint check:** Local `cancelUnreadWebFetchBody` uses `body?.cancel().catch(() => undefined)` (same best-effort pattern as other cancel-unread helpers).
- **Observed result after fix:** `cancelled=true` (non-OK) and `cancel_invoked=true` (readability-off) with `extractor=custom-provider` (see proof log).
- **Fix classification:** Root cause fix

- [x] I understand what the code does
- [x] Change is focused and does not mix unrelated concerns
